title: Unique finite scalar realization of an integral framed extension
statement: Fix the finite datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], a $k$-scheme $T$ and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every integral extension class $\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(i_*\mathbf Z_Z,\mathbf G_m)$, define $b_A(\beta)\in\operatorname{Ext}^2_A(i_*A_Z,A_T(1))$ to be the unique class whose exact abelian realization [def-pur-framed-abelian-realization] is the roots coefficient Yoneda splice [def-pur-framed-scalar-maps]. Existence and uniqueness are part of the characterization, via the supported integral derived-unit bijection; this selects uniquely determined data and imposes no flatness or unramifiedness condition.

source.place: Stacks 03AJ torsors-h1; 03PL Kummer sequence; 0A45 support triangle. Framed-line construction in blueprint main-20261015 lem-pur-divisor-class.proof.md, first sentence and final paragraph.

proof.text: The exponent ell^level is positive by primality of ell, annihilates the coefficient ring, and the coefficient ring is finite. Apply supported_integral_derived_unit to the closed immersion with this exponent and the normalized supported integral generator.

Apply scalar_unit_ext_bijective with target frameTwistEtale T 1 in degree two. Unfold divisorAbelianRealization and divisorRealizeExact to identify its map with the stated exact abelian realization; constantEtale is definitionally ordinaryFiniteConstant.

A bijective function has exactly one preimage of each value (Mathlib Function.Bijective.existsUnique). Apply this to divisorIntegralSplice a i beta. The existing divisorChooseRealization definition then selects the uniquely characterized class, with no alteration of its data.

proof_origin.place: Relative class and Kummer coefficient extension; categorical scalar realization proved using the published supported derived-unit and Ext bijection APIs.
